task: Core #1186 F6-U03u real Supabase Auth/PostgREST read-only two-plan tenant-denial proof; no hosted writes, simulation or fake JWT release.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Critical source-only executable HTTP GET Auth user validation, strict PostgREST Office row grants/denials and unrelated token isolation, with offline mock/non-authority distinction. The current Fresh Install has no Auth users or modern Office 0048, so a live pass is impossible and release remains blocked.

acceptanceCriteria: Pin single Fresh Install HTTPS project and require real Auth /auth/v1/user identity from three distinct externally approved actors; do not accept locally parsed JWT as signature proof.
Run strict readonly PostgREST exact Office thread ID allow/deny matrix for Alap, Pro, revoked-role and anonymous, treating 403/404 and redirects as failures rather than denial proof.
Reject cross-tenant leakage, unknown fields, wrong issuer, user metadata authorization, reused tokens, stale/future expired tokens and missing preapproved fixture IDs.
Positive and fault-injection offline tests exercise matrix but always mark simulated responses as non-authority; production HTTP proof only from explicit approved live GET run.
Exact-head CI, Completion Truth, Lifecycle, stacked DRAFT; no real managed provider/live JWT proven until accounts and Office schema exist.
invariants: GET-only Auth /user and PostgREST; no hosted SQL, user seed, password sign-in, refresh, mutation, staging wake or paid project.
Never publish tokens, service keys, Auth payload or personally identifying response bodies; ensure sanitized proof only.
Provider signed JWT only claims confirmed by Auth /user request matching expected subject, not by decoding token.
Actual remote provider success separate from source-only test closure; no automatic hosted Office release.
forbiddenStates: Mocked fetch accepted as live signed Auth proof.
A 403 permission/404 missing schema accepted as genuine RLS row-denial.
JWT service_role or anonymous user accepted as tenant identity.
Redirect or other host treated as authentic project.
Automatic migration ledger writes or Auth account creation.

failureModes: An attacker fakes reported object counts or swaps project ref while retaining schema fingerprint.
Manifest omits one historical main Office prerequisite or duplicates a baseline 005x migration.
A local 0046 fixture is mistaken for live managed database despite provider-owned Auth/Storage dependencies.
A source digest remains stable but actual hosted Office schema drifts after backup.
Native 31-source forward-only SQL requires irreversible post-commit operations, but recovery key is unavailable.
A release preflight accidentally ships a DB-URL secret or raw private key in Actions logs.
A status falsely becomes READY even though signed-JWT tenant-denial proof and migration ledger are absent.
edgeCases: Migration ledger genuinely has zero rows while the 177-table 0046 schema already exists.
Auth user/office thread counts zero do not mean schema or provider event trigger isolation is unimportant.
Actual clean-source standalone SQL staged without running local-only fixture guard against hosted.
Past artifact valid but source SHA, branch or GitHub run context differs from current exact HEAD.
Backups exclude managed Auth, Storage, role catalog and provider event triggers.
Supavisor session port and TLS root require pinned verification and have distinct semantics from pooler transaction port.
One requested success could be conflated with a different project on the same Supabase organization.

challenge.scenario: Source suffix accidentally contains 30 or 32 originals while comments still mention 31.
challenge.finding: Count assertion and path-marker check alone permit withheld SQL bytes.
challenge.resolution: Byte-level source identity and count and canonical suffix must all match pinned baseline path order.

challenge.scenario: Managed target is silently changed to waterk-platform but both use PostgreSQL17.
challenge.finding: PG major alone is insufficient target attestation.
challenge.resolution: Require literal Fresh project ref plus original 0046 schema and exact target identity.

challenge.scenario: The owner has a ciphertext artifact but has not retained the matching private key outside the assistant workspace.
challenge.resolution: Keep blocked until explicit owner retention and a real decrypt/restore verification contract; never self-attest.

challenge.scenario: CI green native local role simulation misread as deployed Supabase Auth JWT acceptance.
challenge.finding: False positive on private Office permissions and cross-tenant access.
challenge.resolution: Expose providerJwtProven=false, managedApiProven=false, releaseAuthorized=false in immutable output.

challenge.scenario: CI workflow uses a read-only catalog query but later introduces an execute_sql mutation.
challenge.finding: Scope and potentially irreversible DB operations would escape review.
challenge.resolution: No hosted SQL tool in production script; only source package validator and static catalog input.

challenge.scenario: A post-backup schema change occurred after the original read-only catalog was gathered, even though the source original manifest remains pinned.
challenge.finding: A stale managed observation must not release authorize a fresh target.
challenge.resolution: Bind the observation to a read-only Supabase connection with recorded capture timestamp and exact 175+2 legacy fingerprint; a time/source mismatch invalidates the preflight and blocks any SQL release.

challenge.scenario: A planned F6-U03t operator tries to infer full recovery from app-owned public/private pg_dump, leaving Auth, Storage buckets and provider trigger grants outside restore.
challenge.finding: A logical application backup does not provide managed cluster point-in-time recovery or provider service parity.
challenge.resolution: Keep separate provider-managed recovery blockers explicitly, and require owner private-key custody independent of GitHub artifacts.

challenge.scenario: A local test suite claims to cover end-user Office visibility by testing helper functions only without actual provider-issued JWT or managed PostgREST HTTP.
challenge.finding: Testing local role simulation alone permits account and tenant authorization regressions.
challenge.resolution: Always report signedJwtProven=false and managedApiProven=false in this source-only unit and withhold release status until a separate real managed request proof.
